messages.author: e46cb5dd353b7dfb
messages.subject: Re: Modeling Anurans
parts:
Hi Vincent,

You can set it up to model an anuran (or any other wet-skinned animal) by setting the skin wetness parameter 'pct_wet=100'. That will result in an appropriate cutaneous water loss and associated body temperature effect. You can also choose a frog morphology by setting 'shape=4', or just set it up as an ellipse of appropriate dimensions.

I did the pond calculations by setting up the ectotherm model as a container that fills and empties with rainfall. I happen to be working on an update to that just now. I'll provide a vignette on how to use it soon. It's also possible to use the microclimate model to simulate a pond (making the substrate clay, adding a multiplier to the rainfall and setting the parameter 'maxpool' to be the max depth of the pond). There will be some work coming out on this soon.

Note that up until now the ectotherm model available in NicheMapR is really a beta version lacking full documentation. But I've almost finished all of this and will put a formal release out in the next month as well as submitting a software note for publication.

Urtzi Urzelai, Reid Tingley and I have been working on frogs with NicheMapR quite a bit and there'll be a paper coming out in Ecosphere led by Megan Fitzpatrick on freeze/thaw in frogs soon.

All the best,
Mike

messages.author: 54d4981d6bf68eaf
messages.subject: Re: Modeling Anurans
parts:
Hi Vincent,

I have modelled an anuran species (Rana temporaria) with the help of Reid Tingley and Mike. As Mike said, you can model a frog by setting 'pct_wet = 100', and 'shape = 4' (i.e. shape parameters of Lithobates pipiens). You can always manually change those parameters to match the shape of e.g. salamanders.

Then, I used thermal biology data (locomotor performance curves, thermal gradient experiments, and field observations in some cases) to feed relevant parameters that control activity windows to a large extent. These are T_F_min (minimum foraging temperature), T_F_max (maximum foraging temp), T_B_min (maximum basking temp), T_RB_min (minimum temp to go from retreat to basking site), CT_max, CT_min and T_pref. I used the same value for T_F_min, T_B_min, and T_RB_min. That way I simulated a frog that emerged at a given temperature and started foraging immediatelly, because R. temporaria does not thermoregulate through basking. You might also be interested in checking other 'behavioral' parameters (e.g. is your species noctural? crepuscular? how deep are typical retreats? does activity depend on rainfall?). If you have skin resistance to ewl data, I guess that you could also include that by adjusting pct_wet.

I hope this helps. At any rate, if you want to discuss something I am always opened for that.

Good luck with your project!

Cheers,
Urtzi

Hi Vincent!

Regarding metabolic rate, I used the default parameter values of NicheMapR. If you have measured metabolic rates for your species, I would definately use them. However, since ectotherms do not produce (much) heat through metabolism, predictions should not differ that much. But you can always test that! :)
